about.label: — 02 · About the Monument —
about.heading: About the Three Kings Monument
about.lead: A landmark at the heart of Chiang Mai's old city, honouring a great friendship and alliance in Lanna history.
about.entityIntro: Welcome to the Three Kings Monument (พระบรมราชานุสาวรีย์สามกษัตริย์), widely recognized as the central monument of Chiang Mai's old city. Located in the heart of Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, this destination serves as a primary hub for travellers visiting the region.
about.paragraph1: The Three Kings Monument stands in an open square inside the old city walls, in front of the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre (the former Provincial Hall), and marks the start of the famous Sunday Walking Street — a must-see for every visitor.
about.paragraph2: The three bronze statues depict King Mengrai, founder of Chiang Mai; King Ramkhamhaeng the Great of Sukhothai; and King Ngam Muang of Phayao. Legend has it the three kings were close friends and allies who founded Chiang Mai together in 1296.
about.quote: The three kings who founded Chiang Mai remind us of friendship, unity and the wisdom of governance.

history.label: — 03 · History & Legend —
history.heading: History & Legend of the Three Kings
history.intro: In 1296, King Mengrai, together with King Ramkhamhaeng and King Ngam Muang, chose this site to found 'Nopburi Sri Nakhon Ping Chiang Mai'. The monument honours not only the three great kings, but also the friendship and alliance that bound the kingdoms of Lanna, Sukhothai and Phayao together.

pact.title: The Pact of the Three Kings
pact.text: Faced with the rising threat of the Yuan Empire to the north, the three monarchs swore a blood oath by the Ping River — pledging never to attack one another and to stand together in times of peril. This bond of diplomacy secured regional stability and laid the foundation for centuries of Lanna prosperity.

blocks.title: The Founding of Chiang Mai
blocks.text: King Mengrai moved his capital from Wiang Kum Kam to this site, and with the counsel of King Ramkhamhaeng and King Ngam Muang chose this strategic location to found Chiang Mai as the new capital of Lanna.

blocks.title: The Alliance of Three Kingdoms
blocks.text: Lanna, Sukhothai and Phayao were friends and allies, supporting one another in diplomacy and defence. This relationship became the bedrock of long-term regional stability.

blocks.title: An Enduring Legacy
blocks.text: Chiang Mai prospered as the centre of Lanna to this day, and the Three Kings Monument has become the central symbol of the city.

legend.title: The Legend of Friendship
legend.text: Legend has it that the three kings were true friends who consulted one another on every important matter; it was this bond that led to the founding of Chiang Mai.

sevenOmens.title: The Auspicious Omens of Chiang Mai's Founding
sevenOmens.source: Recorded in The Chiang Mai Chronicle

items.title: Sacred Mountain's Embrace
items.text: Doi Suthep shields the west like a natural barrier — excellent feng shui for a capital.

items.title: Two Deer Defy the Hounds
items.text: Two white deer repelled the hunting dogs — a sign that this land could repel its enemies.

items.title: The Mother Mouse Leads Her Young
items.text: A white mouse led five pups into a burrow — symbolising fertility and endless continuity.

items.title: Abundant Waters
items.text: The Ping River and natural springs offered plentiful water for farming and daily life.

didYouKnow.title: Did You Know
didYouKnow.text: The current bronze statues were cast in 1984, replacing the original concrete statues built in 1973–74.

kings.name: King Mengrai
kings.desc: Founder of Chiang Mai and the Lanna Kingdom
kings.story: King Mengrai founded the Lanna Kingdom and, with his two close friends, chose this site to found Chiang Mai as the capital, seeing it as both strategic and rich in resources.

kings.name: King Ramkhamhaeng the Great
kings.desc: Inventor of the Thai script, father of Sukhothai
kings.story: King Ramkhamhaeng is credited with inventing the Thai script and promoting Buddhism. As a close friend of King Mengrai, he gave crucial advice on the founding of Chiang Mai.

kings.name: King Ngam Muang (พญางำเมือง)
kings.desc: The king who ruled Phayao prosperously
kings.story: King Ngam Muang of Phayao was one of the three kings who founded Chiang Mai. Legend tells the three kings were bound by deep friendship and aided one another in times of war and peril.

items.title: Bronze Casting
items.desc: The statues are cast in bronze by skilled artisans; the patina is both beautiful and durable.

items.title: Detail & Proportion
items.desc: Each king's face and attire are finely rendered, conveying individual character.

items.title: Layout in the Open Square

statuePositions.note: The bronze monument was created by a team from Silpakorn University, Thailand's premier arts institution — more than a sculpture, it is regarded as the spiritual pillar of Chiang Mai.

guide.heading: Three Kings Monument Visitor Guide
guide.lead: Key information to plan your visit to the monument in the heart of Chiang Mai's old city.

etiquette.text: Although it is an open public square, locals revere the monument as the spiritual heart of the city. Please dress modestly, do not climb or sit on the base, and avoid mimicking the kings' poses for photos. During festivals, devotees offer marigold garlands (Phuang Malai), candles and even red soda — symbols of vitality and respect.

faqs.q: Is there an entrance fee for the Three Kings Monument?
faqs.a: No — it is free. The monument stands in an open public plaza with no ticket office and no gate, and it can be visited around the clock.
The plaza is open 24 hours a day, every day. Early morning (06:00–08:00) and late afternoon are the most comfortable times to visit.

faqs.q: Where is it, and what are the exact coordinates?
faqs.a: On Prapokklao Road inside the old city, Tambon Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200, Thailand. Plus Code QXRP+3WX · Chiang Mai; coordinates 18.7902° N, 98.9874° E — accurate enough to paste straight into a maps app.

faqs.q: Which three kings does the monument show?
faqs.a: King Mengrai of Lanna, King Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai and King Ngam Muang of Phayao. The statue group commemorates the alliance behind the founding of Chiang Mai in 1296.
Yes. The chronicles describe a pact of friendship between Mengrai, Ramkhamhaeng and Ngam Muang; the monument celebrates that alliance and the founding of the city.
It is in the old-city centre, easily reached on foot from most old-city guesthouses or by red songthaew.

faqs.q: Which landmark is closest, and how far is Wat Phra Singh?
faqs.a: The Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre is directly behind the statue, about a minute on foot. Wat Chedi Luang is about 600 m away and Wat Phra Singh about 750 m — both a short walk.
Please dress modestly and behave respectfully near the statues, especially when taking photos.
From about 16:00 every Sunday the surrounding street becomes the Sunday Walking Street market and part of the road is closed to traffic.

itineraries.title: Old City Day Trip
itineraries.desc: Start at the Three Kings Monument, walk to Wat Phra Singh and Wat Chedi Luang, then end at the Sunday Walking Street.

itineraries.title: Lanna Heritage Route
itineraries.desc: Visit the monument and City Arts & Cultural Centre in the morning, then explore museums and key temples around the old city in the afternoon.

food.label: — 05 · Cultural Triangle —
food.heading: Three Kings Square Cultural Triangle
food.lead: Behind the monument sits Chiang Mai's most important museum cluster — plan to explore them together.

museums.name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre
museums.desc: Immediately behind the statue — exhibitions on Lanna art, history and rotating shows.

museums.name: Lanna Folklife Museum
museums.desc: Directly across the square — traditional Lanna crafts, textiles and daily-life exhibits.

museums.name: Chiang Mai Historical Centre
museums.desc: A short walk away — models and archives tracing the city's 700-year history.

food.comboTicket: Tip: a combined ticket covers several of the museums — budget 1–2 hours for a self-guided cultural walk around the square.

quote.text: The Three Kings Monument is both the starting point of the old-city tour and a favourite gathering place for locals.

landmarks.label: — 03.7 · Location & Surroundings —
landmarks.locationHeading: Location & How to Visit Three Kings Monument in Chiang Mai
landmarks.locationIntro: The Three Kings Monument stands on an open public square on Prapokklao Road, in the historic centre of Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai Province, Thailand (Plus Code QXRP+3WX). It sits inside the old city walls, right in front of the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre, and is easy to reach on foot from most old-city accommodation.
landmarks.heading: Landmarks & Attractions Around Three Kings Monument
landmarks.intro: When visiting the Three Kings Monument, visitors can easily explore the surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest on foot, including Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh.

items.name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre
items.desc: Directly behind the statues in the former provincial hall — Lanna art, history and rotating exhibitions.

items.name: Wat Chedi Luang
items.desc: A landmark temple with a massive ancient chedi, a few minutes to the south-east of the square.

items.name: Wat Phra Singh
items.desc: Home of the revered Phra Singh Buddha image, west along Ratchadamnoen Road.

items.name: Sunday Walking Street
items.desc: Every Sunday from 16:00, Ratchadamnoen Road becomes a pedestrian night market starting right here.
